title: Substring with Concatenation of All Words
description:
You are given a string `s` and an array of strings `words`. All strings in `words` have the same length.

A concatenated string is a string that contains every string in `words` (respecting duplicates) concatenated in any permutation without any intervening characters.

Return a list of all starting indices of concatenated substrings in `s`. You may return the indices in any order.
constraints: All strings in words have the same length.
s and words[i] consist of lowercase English letters.
hints: Because every word has the same length L, any valid match aligns to one of the L residue classes modulo L.
For each starting offset in 0..L-1, slide a word-stepped window across s while tracking the frequency of words currently inside the window.
If a word appears more times than required, advance the left boundary by L until its count is valid again; if an unknown word appears, reset the window past it.

examples.explanation: Substrings "barfoo" at index 0 and "foobar" at index 9 are permutations of ["foo", "bar"].
Every window of length 16 fails to match the exact word multiplicities of ["word", "good", "best", "word"], so return [].
Valid concatenations start at indices 6 ("foobarthe"), 9 ("barthefoo"), and 12 ("thefoobar").
